question: Which arm of a relational ?: does MSC 6.00AX /Og lay out first? With the variable on the left, 'v < K ? A : B' and its mirror 'v >= K ? B : A' compile identically: 'cmp v,K; jl <A>' with the v>=K arm (B) as the fall-through, so for '<' the second arm comes first and for '>=' the first arm comes first. Written constant-left, 'K > v ? A : B' compiles to 'cmp v,K; jge <B>' with A (the K>v arm) first. The arm order in the object is therefore decided by the operand order of the comparison, not by which arm is written first. Positive control root:0F3F DoDigInR (worker resG): 'newattr = 0x30 > (newattr & 0x7f) ? SRand8() + 0x90 : SRand8() + 0xb0' is exact (jge, 0x90 arm first); '(newattr & 0x7f) < 0x30 ? ...' and '(newattr & 0x7f) >= 0x30 ? SRand8() + 0xb0 : ...' both give jl with the 0xb0 arm first (3 bytes differ).
